title: The Stock Market Explained With One Lemonade Stand
alts: When You Buy Apple Stock, Apple Gets $0. Here's Why.
Stocks, IPOs, Bubbles and Short Sellers: One Lemonade Stand
hook: When you buy a share of Apple, Apple doesn't get a cent of your money. So who does? One lemonade stand explains the whole stock market: shares, dividends, IPOs, the market price, bubbles, short selling and crashes.
sources: Apple's IPO: 12 December 1980, 4.6 million shares at $22, raising more than $100 million
Penny's lemonade stand is a made-up example; its numbers are illustrative
tags: stock market explained, how stocks work, what is a share, IPO explained, dividends, market cap, stock bubble, short selling, finance for beginners, lemonade stand
pinned: Penny's business never changed. Only the price did. What would you have done at $1,000 a share?
